question: Should OpenClaw Core permanently own a Pi-to-Review-to-Git-promotion workflow and vendored service-contract runtime, or should Core expose only generic TaskFlow seams while the workflow and contracts live with an owner service/plugin?
rationale: The choice defines durable state ownership, API compatibility, security review scope, package lifecycle behavior, and where future Pi/Review integrations are maintained; it cannot be safely inferred from this external PR alone.

options.title: Keep Core generic
options.body: Retain or improve generic TaskFlow capabilities in Core and move the service-specific workflow, HTTP adapters, Git promotion, and contracts to their owning plugin or service.

options.title: Sponsor a Core platform boundary
options.body: Approve this as a Core product direction, assign an owner and upgrade/security contract, then require a narrower public API, lifecycle policy, and live end-to-end proof before merge.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Leave the PR open only as design reference until the related Pi and Review service owners publish a supported integration contract.

recommendation.title: Keep Core generic
recommendation.body: Retain or improve generic TaskFlow capabilities in Core and move the service-specific workflow, HTTP adapters, Git promotion, and contracts to their owning plugin or service.

likelyOwner.reason: Likely repository-level owner for a Core-versus-service ownership decision; confidence is limited because local feature-history inspection was unavailable in this read-only review environment.
